question: When checking engine compartment belts (such as the alternator, water pump, and power steering belts) for snugness, how much play is acceptable at the center of the belt?
choice_a: Up to 1/4 inch
choice_b: Up to 1/2 inch
choice_c: Up to 3/4 inch
choice_d: Up to 1 inch
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to check belts for snugness, allowing "up to 3/4 inch play at center of belt," along with checking for cracks or frays.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: What is the correct order of steps in the "Safe Start" procedure during the cab check/engine start portion of the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: Start the engine, depress the clutch, then place the gearshift in neutral
choice_b: Depress the clutch, place the gearshift in neutral (or park), start the engine, then release the clutch slowly
choice_c: Place the gearshift in neutral, release the clutch, then start the engine
choice_d: Depress the clutch, start the engine, then release the clutch quickly
explanation: The manual lists the Safe Start steps: "Depress clutch. Place gearshift lever in neutral (or park, for automatic transmissions). Start engine, then release clutch slowly."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: During the cab check, when building air pressure to check the air gauge, to approximately what range should the air compressor build pressure before governor cut-out?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "Build air pressure to governor cut-out, roughly 120-140 psi" when checking the air gauge.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: How many red reflective triangles must a commercial vehicle carry as part of its required emergency equipment?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: Four
explanation: The manual states to "Check for three red reflective triangles, 6 fusees or 3 liquid burning flares."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: For a vehicle equipped with a hydraulic brake reserve (back-up) system, what should the driver do with the key off to check it?
choice_a: Pump the brakes five times and check for air leaks
choice_b: Depress the brake pedal and listen for the sound of the reserve system's electric motor
choice_c: Release the parking brake and confirm the vehicle rolls freely
choice_d: Watch the oil pressure gauge for a normal reading
explanation: The manual states: "with the key off, depress the brake pedal and listen for the sound of the reserve system electric motor."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: During the air brake leakage rate test on a combination vehicle (foot brake fully applied for one minute after the air gauge stabilizes), how much can the air pressure drop before it indicates a problem?
choice_a: No more than 2 pounds
choice_b: No more than 3 pounds
choice_c: No more than 4 pounds
choice_d: No more than 6 pounds
explanation: The manual states to check whether "the air pressure drops more than three pounds in one minute (single vehicle) or four pounds in one minute (combination vehicle) and listen for air leaks."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: How is the service brake check performed during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: Accelerate to 20 mph, brake hard, and measure stopping distance
choice_b: Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and check that the vehicle stops without pulling to either side
choice_c: Apply the parking brake while moving and check for a smooth stop
choice_d: Pump the brake pedal rapidly while stationary and listen for air leaks
explanation: The manual states: "Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake and stop. Check to see that the vehicle does not pull to either side and that it stops when brake is applied."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires versus all other tires during a CDL vehicle inspection?
choice_a: 2/32 inch on steering axle, 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_b: 4/32 inch on steering axle, 2/32 inch on all other tires
choice_c: 6/32 inch on steering axle, 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_d: 4/32 inch on all tires regardless of axle position
explanation: The manual specifies checking "minimum tread depth (4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires)."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: According to the manual, what will NOT earn the applicant credit when checking tire inflation during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: Using a tire gauge
choice_b: Checking that valve caps and stems are not missing or damaged
choice_c: Simply kicking the tires
choice_d: Inspecting for cuts or damage to the tread and sidewalls
explanation: The manual warns: "Note: You will not get credit if you simply kick the tires to check for proper inflation."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: What visible signs on lug nuts may indicate looseness during a wheel inspection?
choice_a: Fresh paint and clean threads
choice_b: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_c: Dull, discolored threads
choice_d: Missing valve caps
explanation: The manual states to check that lug nuts "show no signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: When inspecting a fifth wheel/kingpin coupling, what should the driver verify about the locking jaws?
choice_a: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin
choice_b: That the locking jaws are loosely fitted for easy uncoupling
choice_c: That the locking jaws have been removed for inspection
choice_d: That the locking jaws are visible only from underneath the trailer
explanation: The manual instructs: "Look into fifth wheel gap and check that locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

question: When checking that a semi-trailer is properly seated on the fifth wheel, what should the driver verify about the trailer and skid plate?
choice_a: The trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap
choice_b: There is at least a one-inch gap between the apron and fifth wheel
choice_c: The kingpin protrudes visibly above the fifth wheel skid plate
choice_d: The apron should be disconnected until the tractor is in motion
explanation: The manual states: "Check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate (no gap)."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

topic: Class A Vehicle Inspection Test Versions
question: How many equivalent versions of the Vehicle Inspection test may a Class A CDL applicant be given, and when does the applicant learn which version to perform?
choice_a: Two versions; known in advance
choice_b: Three versions; known at the start of the appointment
choice_c: Four versions; not known until just before testing begins
choice_d: One version; always the same test
explanation: The manual states applicants "will be required to perform one of the four versions of a Vehicle inspection... you will not know which test you will take until just before the testing begins."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-8

question: What does the manual say about a vehicle with components marked or labeled other than by the manufacturer?
choice_a: It must be inspected more thoroughly than usual
choice_b: It cannot be used for the Vehicle Inspection test
choice_c: It receives automatic partial credit
choice_d: The examiner will disregard those components
explanation: The manual states: "Any vehicle that has components marked or labeled, other than by the manufacturer, CANNOT be used for the Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-1

question: When entering or exiting the vehicle during the Vehicle Inspection Test, what safety practice must the applicant follow?
choice_a: Face away from the vehicle and step down quickly
choice_b: Face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times
choice_c: Jump down from the cab to save time
choice_d: Enter and exit only through the passenger-side door
explanation: The manual requires drivers to "safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three (3) points of contact at all times."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-1

question: During the air brake check, before what pressure should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) activate?
choice_a: Below 40 psi
choice_b: Below 55 psi
choice_c: Below 90 psi
choice_d: Below 100 psi
explanation: The manual states: "The low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi or level specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-3

question: In the Emergency Brake(s) Test, within what psi range should the parking (emergency) brake valve close ("pop out") as air pressure continues to be fanned off?
choice_a: Between 5 and 15 psi
choice_b: Between 20 and 45 psi
choice_c: Between 50 and 70 psi
choice_d: Between 80 and 100 psi
explanation: The manual states: "The parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi (no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi)."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-3

question: What happens if an applicant fails to explain and demonstrate all four parts of the air brake check correctly?
choice_a: The examiner deducts points but the test continues
choice_b: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_c: The applicant is given one immediate retry
choice_d: Only a verbal warning is issued
explanation: The manual states: "Failure to explain and demonstrate (perform) all four (4) parts of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-3

question: What is required of the windshield during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: It must be tinted on the upper third only
choice_b: It must be clean with no obstructions except an inspection sticker, and free of cracks or flaws
choice_c: Small cracks are acceptable as long as they don't obstruct direct line of sight
choice_d: It only needs inspection if the vehicle lacks mirrors
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the windshield is clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker. There can be no damage, such as cracks or flaws to the glass."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-2

question: What caution does the manual give regarding the coolant radiator cap during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: Never remove the coolant radiator cap if the engine is hot
choice_b: Always remove the radiator cap before starting the engine
choice_c: The radiator cap should be removed only while the engine is running
choice_d: The radiator cap should never be inspected while the hood is closed
explanation: The manual states: "Caution: Never remove the coolant radiator cap if the engine is hot."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-5

question: When inspecting a trailer's landing gear, what should the applicant check besides that it is fully raised with no missing parts?
choice_a: That the crank handle is secure and, for a tractor semi-trailer, that the fifth wheel is positioned so the tractor frame clears the landing gear during turns
choice_b: That the landing gear is painted the same color as the trailer frame
choice_c: That the landing gear is retracted only halfway for stability
choice_d: That the landing gear has a manufacturer warranty sticker attached
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to inspect that the landing gear "is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure... If tractor semi-trailer, inspect that the fifth wheel is positioned properly so that the tractor frame will clear the landing gear during turns."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-10

topic: School Bus First Aid and Body Fluid Kits
question: What should an applicant check regarding the emergency first aid kit and body fluid cleanup kit on a school bus?
choice_a: That they are present and their seals have not been broken, which may indicate missing items
choice_b: That they were manufactured within the last 30 days
choice_c: That they are stored in the trunk rather than the driver's area
choice_d: That they are painted a bright color for visibility
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that emergency first aid kit is present and the seal has not been broken which may indicate missing items. Inspect that body fluid cleanup kit is present and the seal has not been broken which may indicate missing items."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 11M - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11M-4
